correlations.name: QB passing yards vs that team's top receiver (same game, ex-post leader)
correlations.note: Same plays, so the two legs of a same-game parlay are near-duplicates. The receiver is the ex-post yards leader of that game, not a pregame choice; the QB is the passer with the most attempts in it.

correlations.name: Team passing yards vs top receiver's yards (same game, ex-post leader)
correlations.note: Receiving volume concentrates in the top receiver.

correlations.name: Top-two receivers' yards (same team, same game, ranked ex-post)
correlations.note: Levels move together because the whole passing game expands; the split of targets is a different, zero-sum question (next row).

correlations.name: Top-two receivers' yards, holding team passing volume constant (ex-post ranks)
correlations.note: Partial correlation. This is the part of a same-game pair the market calls 'positive correlation' when you pair two receivers.

correlations.name: Lead RB rushing yards vs team passing yards (same game)
correlations.note: Game script: trailing teams abandon the run.

correlations.name: Lead RB rushing yards vs top receiver's yards (same team, same game, ex-post leaders)
correlations.note: The classic 'one man eats' problem inside a same-game parlay.

correlations.name: A player's own receptions vs own receiving yards (same game)
correlations.note: Same player, two props. Effectively one leg priced twice.

correlations.name: Home QB passing yards vs away QB passing yards (same game)
correlations.note: Pace and shootout games lift both sides: this is the one useful positive cross-team correlation.

correlations.name: Total receiving yards, home vs away (same game)
correlations.note: Game environment, measured without using the result.

correlations.name: Home margin vs game total (completed games)
correlations.note: Margin and total are close to orthogonal, which is why spread+total combos add little risk.

correlations.name: Closing spread vs closing total
correlations.note: The two prices are quoted almost independently.

correlations.name: Home ATS result vs game total, same game
correlations.note: Settlement-level independence for a cross-market same-game parlay.

qb_plus_wr1.selection: Descriptive full-sample example. Thresholds are whole-sample medians and the receiver is the ex-post yards leader, so this is NOT a pregame strategy and NOT a priced sportsbook offer (issue #19). No prop price is attached to it anywhere.
qb_plus_wr1.note: Legs are close to the same event, so a book that priced them independently would lose; real books shorten same-game prices.

wr1_plus_wr2.note: Two receivers on one team compete for the same targets.

cross_game.note: Lag-1 autocorrelation of the weekly mean margin and of the weekly home cover rate (pushes excluded from the rate). Near-zero values are consistent with week-to-week outcomes not carrying over, but this does not establish contemporaneous cross-game independence: pairwise independence does not imply joint independence of a multi-leg ticket.

coverage.note: Built from nflverse player-week extracts, which are aggregations of the NFL's official play-by-play.
